test_title: Delhi Police Constable (Executive) 2023 - GK/CA (Held on: 16 Nov, 2023 Shift 1)
subject: gk
question: Which of the following is NOT a fundamental duty?

options.text: To value and preserve the rich heritage of the country’s composite culture
To uphold and protect the sovereignty, unity and integrity of India

solution:
The correct answer is __**To promote cooperative society**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__

• The Constitution of India specifies certain duties that every citizen is expected to perform, known as Fundamental Duties.

• These duties are enshrined in Part IV-A of the Indian Constitution under Article 51A.

• Promoting a cooperative society is not listed among the Fundamental Duties.

• Fundamental Duties were added to the Constitution by the 42nd Amendment in 1976, based on the recommendations of the Swaran Singh Committee.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Fundamental Duties**

• Fundamental Duties are moral obligations of all citizens to help promote a spirit of patriotism and to uphold the unity of India.

• There are 11 Fundamental Duties listed in the Indian Constitution.

• These include duties such as respecting the National Flag and National Anthem, cherishing the noble ideals of freedom struggle, protecting the sovereignty and integrity of India, promoting harmony, and safeguarding public property.

• **42nd Amendment Act, 1976**

• This amendment is also known as the Mini-Constitution due to the large number of changes it brought about in the Indian Constitution.

• It added ten Fundamental Duties to the Constitution under Article 51A.

• The act also made changes to various other parts of the Constitution, including the Preamble, Fundamental Rights, and Directive Principles of State Policy.

• **Swaran Singh Committee**

• The committee was set up in 1976 by the Indian government to make recommendations on Fundamental Duties and other constitutional amendments.

• It was chaired by Dr. Swaran Singh, who was a former Minister of External Affairs.

• The committee's recommendations led to the inclusion of Fundamental Duties in the Indian Constitution through the 42nd Amendment.
